Multiple 
Sclerosis
NRBS 4210 - Group 5A
Stephanie Russell-Kraft, Julia Galasso, Jessie Zheng, Abraham Pessin, 
Kaitlyn Benjamin, Sophia Bruno, Ejiogu Ifeanyi

What is Multiple 
Sclerosis (MS)?
• A progressive, demyelinating, autoimmune disease of 
the central nervous system (CNS)
• The exact cause of MS is unknown
• Progressive demyelination disrupts the flow of nerve 
impulses and causes the formation of lesions or 
plaques on the brain and spinal cord
• Most frequently affected areas include the optic 
nerves, chiasm, and tracts; the cerebrum; the 
brainstem and cerebellum; and the spinal cord 
• These lesions can sometimes  be seen on MRI

Risk Factors & 
Early Detection
• No known risk factors but a higher risk of developing MS is 
associated with:
⚬ Female sex (affects females 3x as much as males)
⚬ Vitamin D deficiency
⚬ History of Epstein-Barr Virus infection 
⚬ Living in higher northern latitudes
⚬ Smoking
⚬ Obesity 
• Early detection is key in diagnosis 
• Most commonly diagnosed between ages 20-50
• The goal of treatment is to slow progression of the disease
*There are currently no known measures 
to prevent disease progression*

Clinical 
Manifestations
• Many symptoms are characteristic of MS:
⚬ Vision changes (sudden decrease/loss, 
blurred, double vision)
⚬ Numbness, tingling, or sensory loss in 
body or limbs
⚬ Changes in balance or coordination       
⚬ Spasticity, ataxia, tremor
⚬ Fatigue, weakness in arms or legs
⚬ Pain (patients may need daily 
analgesics)
⚬ Heat sensitivity (which may trigger the 
above)
⚬ Three main clinical MS phenotypes:
￭ Relapsing-remitting (RRMS)
• 85% of patients
• Symptoms come in waves of “attacks” and 
recovery periods, with a gradual decline in 
function over time
￭ Secondary progressive (SPMS)
• Disease progression with or without relapses
• Most RRMS patients eventually progress to 
this form
￭ Primary progressive (PPMS)
• 15% of patients
• Steady increase in neurologic disability
⚬ Radiology-isolated syndrome (RIS)
￭ MS-type lesions are found on an MRI
￭ No clinical signs or symptoms

Diagnostic Tests & 
Nursing responsibilities
Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)
• MRI can show myelin plaques on the brain 
and spine.
• Nursing consideration: metal safety 
assessment (some patients may not be 
eligible for all MRI types)
Lumbar puncture (LP)
• Lumbar puncture collects CSF which 
can show oligoclonal banding
• Nursing considerations
⚬ Ensure proper positioning of 
patient to allow for easier access 
to spinal canal to collect 
cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) & 
promote pt comfort as much as 
possible
⚬ Have patient lie down for at least 
30 minutes after LP and educate 
them to drink a lot of fluid for at 
least 24 hrs after procedure

Medical Management
• There is no cure for MS, but treatments can relieve symptoms or slow the progression of MS.

• Disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) prevent 
the formation of further lesions/plaques.
⚬ oral DMTs: fingolimod, diroximel fumarate, 
dimethyl fumarate, siponimod.
⚬ infusion DMTs: ocrelizumab, natalizumab.
⚬ injection DMTs: interferon, glatiramer 
acetate.

Nursing Considerations 
for Medical Management
• MS patients should get annual MRIs for monitoring.
⚬ Nurses can encourage follow-up care
• Many DMTs are immunomodulators - patients should be educated to 
avoid crowds, stay away from those who are sick, avoid raw food, etc.
⚬ Advise patients to discuss all potential vaccinations with their 
provider, as some live vaccines may be contraindicated.
Mri
• Additional nursing considerations:
⚬ Assist with coping, provide support to patient and family
⚬ Promote physical mobility, assist with gentle exercises and ROM exercises
⚬ Avoid hot baths and ice packs
⚬ Fall prevention - gait training, assistive devices
⚬ Nutrition - healthy eating and weight reduction
⚬ Manage fatigue - monitor medication side effects
⚬ Educate patients about self-care

Patient & Family Education
Discharge Planning & Homecare
• Report new or worsening symptoms:  weakness, numbness, vision changes, balance 
problems, bowel/bladder changes, pain or severe fatigue
• Seek urgent care  for sudden severe neurologic changes, major vision loss, difficulty 
swallowing, fever or signs of infection
• Keep follow-up appointments  for neurologic evaluations, labs and scheduled MRIs
• Avoid overheating:  use cool showers, lightweight clothing, air conditioning and rest 
in a cool environment
• Manage fatigue:  pace activities, schedule rest periods, simplify tasks and ask for 
help 
• Prevent falls: continue PT/stretching, use prescribed assistive devices and remove 
home hazards such as throw rugs, clutter and loose cords
• Encourage family support/involvement, counseling and MS support groups

NCLEX Style 
Question 1
A nurse is providing teaching to a client who has a new diagnosis 
of multiple sclerosis (MS). The client asks the nurse about the 
usual course of MS. Which of the following responses should the 
nurse make?
A. "Each client is different; we cannot predict what will happen."
B. "I can see that you are worried, but it’s too soon to predict what will happen."
C. "Acute episodes are usually followed by remissions, which can vary in duration."
D. "It’s too early to think about the future; let’s focus on the present and take each day 
as it comes."

NCLEX Style 
Question 1
A nurse is providing teaching to a client who has a new diagnosis 
of multiple sclerosis (MS). The client asks the nurse about the 
usual course of MS. Which of the following responses should the 
nurse make?
A. "Each client is different; we cannot predict what will happen."
B. "I can see that you are worried, but it’s too soon to predict what will happen."
C. "Acute episodes are usually followed by remissions, which can vary in duration. "
D. "It’s too early to think about the future; let’s focus on the present and take each day 
as it comes."
Rationale: MS is a chronic autoimmune disorder that is characterized by remissions and exacerbations. The 
client is asking for information, so the nurse should inform the client that as the disease progresses, 
exacerbations tend to become more frequent and intense.

NCLEX Style 
Question 2
The nurse has been educating a client newly diagnosed with MS. 
Which of the following statements by the client indicates an 
understanding of the education? 
A. “I should complete my exercises quickly to reduce fatigue.”
B. “I should participate in non–weight-bearing exercises.”
C. “I will take hot tub baths to decrease spasms.”
D. “I will stretch daily as directed by the physical therapist.”

NCLEX Style 
Question 2
The nurse has been educating a client newly diagnosed with MS. 
Which of the following statements by the client indicates an 
understanding of the education? 
A. “I should complete my exercises quickly to reduce fatigue.”
B. “I should participate in non–weight-bearing exercises.”
C. “I will take hot tub baths to decrease spasms.”
D. “I will stretch daily as directed by the physical therapist. ”
Rationale: Daily stretching is crucial for multiple sclerosis patients to maintain joint mobility, increase 
flexibility, and prevent contractures or muscle spasticity. Following the guidance of a physical therapist 
ensures safety and efficacy of the routine.
